text:
maria (infra-oncall): New GPU node pool in eu-west-1 failing to finish bootstrap. kubelet stuck at image pull step, lots of ECR timeouts in the node init logs. Any quick ideas? :thinking_face:

sam (eng-sre): Seeing alerts too. A few nodes show `Get "https://******.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/...": dial tcp: i/o timeout` in cloud-init logs.

lee (netops): Did we recently change TGW route propagations or add a VPC route? Those usually bite return path for interface endpoints.

maria (infra-oncall): Not that I'm aware of — we did a one-off TGW attachment change yesterday for the analytics VPC. Could that affect this VPC?

sam (eng-sre): Paste of the curl from a broken node namespace (from init container):
```
curl -v https://******.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/v2/ -m 10
* Connected to ******.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com (10.0.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* Connected to 10.0.12.34 (10.0.12.34) port 443
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 10000 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

lee (netops): That IP looks like an interface endpoint ENI IP. So DNS resolved to VPCE ENI. Good. But timeout suggests return traffic might be leaving VPC via wrong path or SG on the VPCE ENI blocking. Can you dump route table for the subnet?

maria (infra-oncall): Route table for subnet-0a:
```
Route Table: rtb-0abcde
Destination      Target
10.0.0.0/16      local
0.0.0.0/0        nat-0aaabbbccc
10.10.0.0/16     tgw-attach-0ffff   (propagated)
```

sam (eng-sre): Wait — 10.10.0.0/16 is the analytics VPC. That route is fine. The interface endpoint ENIs are in 10.0.12.0/24 though.

lee (netops): Can we see the VPC route table entries visible from TGW side? My hunch: TGW propagation added a more specific route that accidentally matches the ENI traffic or reverse path.

alice (platform): Quick check: interface endpoint SG inbound is open only for 443 from the VPC CIDR (10.0.0.0/16). The endpoint ENIs themselves are associated with that SG. If return traffic leaves via TGW to analytics and comes back from another AZ, the source port mapping might be off?

maria (infra-oncall): I pulled the flow logs for a failed pull. Here's the relevant line (redacted):
```
10.0.11.45 -> 10.0.12.34 TCP 443 REJ
```
It shows REJ instead of ACCEPT on ENI 10.0.12.34.

lee (netops): Why is the ENI rejecting? Check the endpoint's SG ingress rules and NACLs for the subnet hosting the ENI.

sam (eng-sre): SG on VPCE: inbound 443 from 10.0.0.0/16. Node source IP is 10.0.11.45 so it should match. NACLs are default ALLOW.

maria (infra-oncall): Another weirdness: packets from node -> endpoint arrive, but endpoint's reply goes out via TGW attachment because route propagation on the TGW added a 10.0.12.0/24 route pointing to TGW (prop mistakenly accepted). That causes asymmetric routing and the endpoint SG treats the connection as invalid and rejects.

lee (netops): Bingo. I can see in TGW route table a propagated route for 10.0.12.0/24 learned from the analytics attachment due to a misconfigured advertisement. That makes TGW the next-hop for ENI subnets. Since interface endpoint ENIs are local to the VPC, return traffic must stay local. Asymmetric path -> stateful SG sees unexpected src/dst pairs and REJ.

maria (infra-oncall): So root cause = TGW propagation created a more specific route that hijacked traffic for endpoint ENIs, causing egress to go to TGW and back out, breaking the endpoint connections.

alice (platform): Quick mitigation options: 1) remove the propagated 10.0.12.0/24 route from the TGW attachment (preferred), 2) add a more specific local route on the VPC RT to force ENI-local traffic, or 3) temporarily route node egress via NAT in same AZ while we fix TGW.

sam (eng-sre): I removed the propagation entry from the TGW (asked network team to withdraw). Retrying bootstrap on a new node now.

deploy-bot: New node autoscale request queued -> instance i-0f12345 starting (eu-west-1a).

maria (infra-oncall): Node provisioned and completed image pulls. kubelet ready. Tests green. :tada:

lee (netops): Filing follow-up: make TGW route propagation audit run as a daily check and add an alert for any propagated route that overlaps VPC /24s that host interface endpoints.

alice (platform): Also adding a preflight check in the node bootstrap that resolves ECR endpoints to ENI IPs and tests TLS handshake before letting ASG consider the instance healthy.

maria (infra-oncall): Thanks all. Root cause summary for postmortem: asymmetric routing caused by TGW propagated route for ENI subnets -> interface endpoint connections rejected -> image pulls time out -> node provisioning fails.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2345. Assigned to netops.

sam (eng-sre): Small takeaway: interface endpoints depend on symmetric local routing. If you change TGW propagation or route advertisement, check for accidental /24s that overlap ENI subnets.

lee (netops): Adding runbook entry: when adding TGW attachments, block propagation of subnets that host VPCE ENIs or use route filters.

maria (infra-oncall): Closing thread — follow-ups logged. :white_check_mark:
